plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with large, daisy-like flower heads made of golden ray florets around a dark central disc. Heads track the sun when young. Widely grown as an ornamental and for seeds and oil.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early autumn (July to September) in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to North America; cultivated worldwide, especially in the United States, Ukraine, Russia, and France
plants.funFact: Young sunflower buds follow the sun from east to west each day, a movement called heliotropism, but mature flowers face east and stop moving.

plants.name: Calluna vulgaris
plants.description: A low, evergreen shrub that carpets moorlands and heaths with tiny bell-shaped flowers in dense spikes. It thrives in acidic, nutrient-poor soils and is vital for bees and grouse.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Moorlands and heaths of Scotland, northern England, Scandinavia, and across Europe; naturalized in parts of North America
plants.funFact: Heather honey is prized for its jelly-like texture, and the plant has historically been used for thatching, bedding, and brewing ale.

plants.name: Solidago canadensis
plants.description: A tall perennial wildflower producing arching plumes of tiny golden flower heads. It spreads by rhizomes and forms large colonies in meadows, roadsides, and open fields. It is an important late-season nectar source for pollinators.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (July to October)
plants.location: Native to North America, from Canada through the northern United States; invasive in parts of Europe and Asia
plants.funFact: Goldenrod is often blamed for hay fever, but its pollen is heavy and insect-carried; the real culprit is usually ragweed blooming at the same time.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A striking evergreen shrub with the largest flower head in the protea family, up to 30 cm across, with a bowl of pink-tipped bracts surrounding a fuzzy center. It is South Africa's national flower and is adapted to fire-prone fynbos.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring in the Southern Hemisphere, with flowering peaking from August to November
plants.location: Fynbos of the Western and Eastern Cape, South Africa; cultivated in Australia, Hawaii, and California
plants.funFact: Proteas are ancient flowering plants dating back about 300 million years, and their name comes from the Greek god Proteus, who could change shape.
